newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE THRASH VICTORIA IN TOUR OPENER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE THRASH VICTORIA IN TOUR OPENER.

text.p: France opened their short rugby union tour to Australia by scoring eleven tries in a 65-13 romp against a weak Victoria side on Tuesday.
Centre Richard Dourthe led the rampage with three tries and five conversions for a personal tally of 25 points at Olympic Park.
But the match proved of little value as a form guide for the two-test series against the Wallabies later this month given the lack of pace and experience in the amateur Victoria side.
On several occasions, the tourists opted to run the ball from deep in defence, most notably when 10 players combined in a move spanning the entire length of the pitch for their second try.
Assistant coach Pierre Villepreux said such extravagant play would not be confined to tour matches against the weaker state teams.
"We have this philosophy that we want to play this type of game not only against Victoria but also at higher levels," Villepreux said.
"If the situation (is there) to run the ball from your own try line, why not."
France meet Australia in the first test in Sydney on June 21 with the second a week later in Brisbane.
Winger Sebastien Viars added two tries for France, who led 34-8 at halftime.

Their other tries were scored by centres Thomas Castaignede and Christophe Lamaison, a second half replacement, winger Pierre Bondouy, flyhalf David Aucagne, flanker Olivier Magne, and number eight Pierre Raschi.

Victoria enjoyed their best moment in the second minute when centre Matthew Nasalio was first to reach a kick through by flyhalf Andrew Hendry to give the home side an improbable and short-lived lead.
Hendry kicked a penalty before halftime before Nasalio scored a second consolation try late in the game.

France - 15-Nicholas Brusque; 14-Sebastien Viars, 13-Richard Dourthe, 12-Thomas Castaignede (Christophe Lamaison), 11-Pierre Bondouy; 10-David Aucagne, 9-Guy Accoceberry (captain); 8-Pierre Raschi, 7-Richard Castel, 6-Olivier Magne, 5-Olivier Merle, 4-Thiery Cleda, 3-David L'Aperne, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Christian Califano.

Victoria - 15-Anton Pilli; 14-Paul Ioane, 13-Matthew Nasalio, 12-Lachlan Strauss, 11-Garvan Low; 10-Andrew Hendry, 9-Luke Daley; 8-Nata Urika, 7-Jason Deans, 6-Cameron Frater, 5-Tony Booth, 4-Brenton Parsons, 3-Stavros Iakodvidis, 2-Darryl Thompson (captain), 1-Andrew Charles
